amendments.normalized_body: Add validation for `chloride_protection_factor` in `validate_shrimp_runtime_params()` (invariants.rs). Currently `critical_molt_gh_ratio`, `molt_success_threshold`, and all other named shrimp parameters are validated, but `chloride_protection_factor` has no bounds check. A negative or NaN value would silently break the hazard formula (the `.max(0.0)` inside `compute_effective_nitrite_hazard` handles negatives at runtime, but NaN/Infinity would propagate). Add `check_non_negative("shrimp_params.chloride_protection_factor", params.chloride_protection_factor)?;` alongside the existing parameter checks, and add a corresponding invalid-value test case to the `malformed_current_save_with_invalid_molt_mineral_parameters_is_rejected` and `step_hours_rejects_invalid_molt_mineral_parameters_before_simulation` tests.

In `salt_treatment_source_profile()` (tests/shrimp_chloride_protection.rs:69-89), the helper constructs a `SourceWaterProfile` using `WaterState::default_for_volume_l(1.0)` to extract per-liter defaults. Several fields use `base.<field>_total` as concentrations, which works only because volume is 1.0L. The `bicarbonate_mg_total` field in particular is solver-derived and initialized to 0.0 in `default_for_volume_l` before `resolve_carbonate_state` runs, so the profile's `bicarbonate_mg_per_l` will be whatever the solver yields for 1L — not a clean default. Add a brief inline comment documenting the 1L-total-equals-concentration pattern to prevent confusion in future maintenance, or consider using explicit numeric constants instead of extracting from the WaterState.

Implement the actual chloride-aware nitrite hazard requested by tanksim-6e5.6.5 before merging. The current patch only adds alkalinity bookkeeping/tracing in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:12-23,366-385`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:10-27,335-338`, and related budget helpers, while the shrimp nitrite path is still the old chloride-blind logic in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:18-43,274-315,748-773`. There is still no `chloride_protection_factor`, no chloride-adjusted effective hazard, and no integration into `hourly_nitrite_stress_accum`, so equal-NO2 scenarios with different chloride levels will behave identically and the bead’s acceptance criteria are still unmet.

If the alkalinity budget work is intentional, extend the runtime budget guard to validate alkalinity too. The patch promotes alkalinity to a first-class tracked quantity in `crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:68-123` and exposes it through inspection/debug helpers in `crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:64-203,418-478,533-640`, but `enforce_tracked_tick_budget_guard` still only checks nitrogen and carbon in `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:845-909`. That leaves the new alkalinity accounting informational only: future stage bugs or incorrect explicit deltas can silently drift alkalinity without tripping the engine’s safety check.
